purpose: This is a small device used to inject insulin just under your skin to help control your blood sugar levels. It is commonly used by people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. The device is pre-set to deliver a dose of up to 30 units of insulin safely and consistently.
how_it_works: When you have diabetes, your body either does not make enough insulin or does not use it well, causing your blood sugar to rise too high. This device delivers insulin directly under the skin (subcutaneous tissue), where it is absorbed into your bloodstream. Once in your blood, insulin helps move sugar from your blood into your body's cells for energy, bringing your blood sugar back to a safer level.
common_side_effects: The most common issue is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, sweaty, dizzy, or confused. You may also notice redness, swelling, or a small bump at the injection site. Rotating where you inject can help reduce skin irritation.
warnings: Never share your insulin device or needles with anyone else — this can spread serious infections. Watch carefully for signs of low blood sugar and always have a fast-acting sugar source nearby like juice or glucose tablets. Talk to your doctor before changing your dose. Store insulin properly as directed and check expiration dates. If you are sick, stressed, or your routine changes, your insulin needs may change — contact your healthcare provider.
typical_dosing: Your doctor will tell you exactly how many units to take and when. This device holds up to 30 units per injection. Dosing is very personal and depends on your blood sugar levels, meals, and activity. Never adjust your dose on your own without guidance from your healthcare team.
